subject: mitosis

composition.story: What happens during mitosis? Start after DNA copying. Follow chromosome copies as they condense, align, and separate. Compare the new nuclei: each receives a matching chromosome set. Use Previous and Next to inspect each stage.

aha.observation: Each new nucleus receives an A copy and a B copy because sister copies separate toward opposite poles.

parts.presentation: Place below the explanation and above the experiment. Use short rail labels and show the full active stage name. Keep progress on this rail.

Use the canonical mitosis composition with a fixed cell boundary. Region phases follow the active rail index in variant.states order. Highlight state.active. Keep chromosome labels visible throughout. Compare the final nuclei side by side at a shared scale. A copies use a solid pattern; B copies use a striped pattern. Assume an idealized animal cell with chromosomes A and B, already replicated. No DNA synthesis, chromosome errors, or cytokinesis occurs here. Copy names identify their eventual pole, not an additional process. Keep all labels readable at native width.
Anchor beside the named target without covering chromosomes. Identify the relevant location and mechanism; leave measurements in the readouts.

Place counts below the picture, followed by the bound status line. A DNA copy means one chromatid-sized DNA molecule, including joined sisters. Counts are exact integers, not chromosome counts. Left and right groups refer to opposite spindle poles. An em dash means no separated group exists. Balanced parameter-control budget: zero; navigation and Reset are separate.

states.label: Before mitosis
states.sentence: Inside the Nuclear envelopes, A-left copy and A-right copy are joined sisters; B-left copy and B-right copy are also joined sisters.
states.why: DNA copying has already occurred; mitosis will distribute these existing copies.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: DNA copied; sister copies remain joined.

states.label: Prophase
states.sentence: A-left copy, A-right copy, B-left copy, and B-right copy condense into visible chromosome pairs while the Spindle forms.
states.why: Condensation packages the DNA; sister copies remain joined.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Chromosomes condense; DNA-copy total stays unchanged.

states.label: Prometaphase
states.sentence: The Nuclear envelopes break down, allowing the Spindle to attach opposite sisters to opposite poles.
states.why: Opposing attachments prepare each sister pair for separation.

states.label: Metaphase
states.sentence: The Spindle holds the A and B sister pairs at the cell equator, with opposite sisters attached toward opposite poles.
states.why: Each pole is connected to a copy of every chromosome type.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Sister pairs align; copies remain joined.

states.label: Anaphase
states.sentence: The Spindle separates A-left copy and B-left copy from A-right copy and B-right copy toward opposite poles.
states.why: Released sister copies become independent chromosomes; separation redistributes DNA without making more.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Matching chromosome groups reach opposite poles.

states.label: Telophase
states.sentence: The Nuclear envelopes re-form around matching A and B sets; chromosome copies decondense and the Spindle disassembles.
states.why: Compare the new nuclei: each contains the same chromosome types. Cytokinesis divides the cell and is not shown.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Mitosis has produced matching chromosome sets in separate nuclei.
